info.name: Public Sector Backend
info.description:
Full API coverage for the public-sector-backend NestJS app: Phase 1 auth (Admin/Agent/Client), the Governance Bundle (sessions, invites, audit log), and Document Ingestion Infrastructure.

Organized into four top-level groups (Admin, Agent, IPPIS, Client) plus a standalone Health check. Each group is self-contained: it has its own Auth (where applicable) and its own Session sub-folder using that group's own tokens, so you can run a whole group top-to-bottom without reaching into another group. Admin's 'Force-Revoke Sessions' (which targets an Agent's or a Client's sessions) stays under Admin since it's an admin-performed action, even though its target is an Agent/Client — it does not change how Agent/Client manage their own sessions.

Each endpoint has multiple requests: at least one success scenario and the meaningful failure scenarios (validation, auth, permission, not-found). Success requests have test scripts that capture tokens/ids into collection variables so later requests in the same folder (or run via Collection Runner) chain automatically.

MAINTENANCE: this collection must be kept in sync with the codebase. See ../CLAUDE.md and postman/README.md for the standing rule — any change to a controller, DTO, or permission key must be reflected here in the same change.

On success, force-revokes every existing session for that admin, so admin_access_token/admin_refresh_token from a prior login will stop working.

request.description: Voluntary password change for the currently logged-in admin (admin_access_token) — unlike reset-password, this does not revoke other sessions. On success, updates the admin_password collection variable so subsequent requests (e.g. a later login) keep working.

Begins TOTP enrollment for the currently logged-in admin (admin_access_token) — returns a base32 secret and an otpauth:// URI to enter into an authenticator app. Nothing is enabled yet until a real generated code is confirmed via 'POST /auth/admin/2fa/confirm - Success'. 409 if this admin already has 2FA enabled (see 'POST /auth/admin/2fa/setup - Already enabled (409)'). On success, captures the secret into the admin_2fa_secret collection variable.

exec: pm.test('returns TOTP secret and otpauth URL', () => { pm.expect(json.method).to.eql('TOTP'); pm.expect(json.secret).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(json.otpauthUrl).to.be.a('string'); });

originalRequest.description: Begins TOTP enrollment for the currently logged-in admin (admin_access_token) — returns a base32 secret and an otpauth:// URI to enter into an authenticator app. Nothing is enabled yet until a real generated code is confirmed via 'POST /auth/admin/2fa/confirm - Success'. 409 if this admin already has 2FA enabled (see 'POST /auth/admin/2fa/setup - Already enabled (409)'). On success, captures the secret into the admin_2fa_secret collection variable.

request.description: Begins EMAIL 2FA enrollment — emails a 6-digit verification code via the (mock console) email provider. Check the running server's console log for a line like 'Email to ... — Your two-factor setup code\nYour verification code is: <code>', then paste it into the admin_2fa_code collection variable before running 'POST /auth/admin/2fa/confirm - Success'.

originalRequest.description: Begins EMAIL 2FA enrollment — emails a 6-digit verification code via the (mock console) email provider. request.description: Run this after 2FA has already been confirmed as enabled for admin_access_token's admin (e.g. after 'POST /auth/admin/2fa/confirm - Success') — setup is rejected once 2FA is already active, regardless of which method is requested.

request.description: Activates 2FA using a real code — for TOTP, generate one from the admin_2fa_secret collection variable (an authenticator app, or 'otplib'/'generate({ secret })'); for EMAIL, use the code captured from the console-logged setup email. Paste the code into the admin_2fa_code collection variable first. Only activates on a real, successfully-verified code, so a botched setup never locks anyone out.

request.description: Disables 2FA for the currently logged-in admin (admin_access_token) once it's enabled — requires re-confirming the current password. Unlike reset-password, this does not revoke other sessions.

request.description: A variant of 'POST /auth/admin/login - Success' showing the response shape once 2FA is enabled for this admin — real tokens are withheld and a short-lived pendingToken is returned instead. Run this after 2FA has been confirmed as enabled (e.g. via the TOTP setup+confirm requests above). On success, captures the pendingToken into the admin_2fa_pending_token collection variable for 'POST /auth/admin/2fa/login-verify - Success'.

originalRequest.description: A variant of 'POST /auth/admin/login - Success' showing the response shape once 2FA is enabled for this admin — real tokens are withheld and a short-lived pendingToken is returned instead. Run this after 2FA has been confirmed as enabled (e.g. via the TOTP setup+confirm requests above). request.description: Completes a 2FA-gated login using the pendingToken captured from 'POST /auth/admin/login - Two-factor required' and a fresh real code (generate a new one from admin_2fa_secret for TOTP, since a previously-used code may already be stale) — issues real tokens exactly like a normal login. pendingToken is signed with a separate secret (JWT_TWO_FACTOR_PENDING_SECRET), so it cannot be used as a real Bearer token anywhere.

originalRequest.description: Completes a 2FA-gated login using the pendingToken captured from 'POST /auth/admin/login - Two-factor required' and a fresh real code (generate a new one from admin_2fa_secret for TOTP, since a previously-used code may already be stale) — issues real tokens exactly like a normal login. pendingToken is signed with a separate secret (JWT_TWO_FACTOR_PENDING_SECRET), so it cannot be used as a real Bearer token anywhere.

request.description: A wrong code is rejected without invalidating the pending token — admin_2fa_pending_token can still be retried with a correct code afterward (see 'POST /auth/admin/2fa/login-verify - Success').
